evidence: Full head-to-toe check at 07:25: no injury, no pain, observations normal. GP reviewed at 11:00 and found no injury. No treatment needed.
summary: E.W. tripped on a bath mat while walking to the bathroom with a care worker beside her, as her care plan required. She was lowered gently to the floor. No injury or pain; GP found no injury and no treatment was needed. Bath mat replaced.

evidence: Staff called police at 15:30 and reported R.T. missing.
summary: R.T. left the unit through a gate propped open by a contractor. Police were called and found him at a bus stop 2 km away, cold and confused but unhurt.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: M.K. said "he grabbed me hard last night when I didn't want to get up". One care worker assisted M.K. with a transfer at about 02:00.
summary: Resident alleged a care worker grabbed her forearms hard during a 02:00 transfer, causing new bruising. GP prescribed pain relief and dressings; the care worker was stood down pending investigation.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: The safe access log shows one staff member opened it on each of the four days.
summary: J.P.'s daughter reported four unauthorised cash withdrawals totalling $240 from J.P.'s bank card kept in the facility safe. Safe access logs show one staff member opened the safe on each of the four withdrawal days. Staff member stood down.
priority_reasons: reasonable grounds to report to police

evidence: The night agency nurse raised both bed rails for D.L. overnight "to stop him wandering". D.L. has no assessment, consent or behaviour support plan for bed rails.
summary: Agency nurse raised both bed rails overnight to prevent wandering without assessment, consent, or behaviour support plan. Rails lowered at 06:00. No injury or distress.

evidence: A.N. requires minced and moist meals under her speech pathologist's plan. At lunch she was served a regular-texture roast.
summary: Resident on a speech pathologist minced and moist meal plan was served a regular-texture roast. She coughed on the first mouthful. Staff removed the meal; RN assessed no treatment needed. Correct meal was then served.
